title: Ghosts, pasties and tarot made this Bolton fundraiser one to remember
excerpt: Para-Northern Investigations’ Bolton paranormal charity night featuring the Warrens’ grandson raises £740.57 for Sands, with talks, tarot, quiz, raffle and food.
content:
A paranormal charity night featuring the grandson of two world-famous ghost investigators has raised more than £740 for Sands.

Para-Northern Investigations held the fundraiser at Dunscar Golf Club, with organiser Emma Flood confirming the night raised £740.57 for the stillbirth and neonatal death charity.

Emma said that "it was a fantastic night" that brought together paranormal enthusiasts for an evening of talks, a quiz, tarot readings, a raffle and food, with a number of prizes up for grabs.

She added: “We absolutely loved it and we were so happy so many of you came to show your support.

“The room was filled with laughter and fun and it was great to see.”

Among those involved was Chris McKinnell, grandson of American paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren.

The Warrens became internationally known for their investigations into alleged hauntings, with cases connected to the couple later inspiring films including The Conjuring.

Chris appeared at the Bolton fundraiser via video link.

Jamie Williams also appeared during the night, speaking about Mill Street Barracks and its reported paranormal activity.

Jamie Williams and Emma Flood

The evening also featured a paranormal quiz hosted by Maura Jackson and tarot readings from Gemma Nuttall, while Burnden Pie Shop provided food.

Maura Jackson hosted the spooky quiz

Some substantial prizes were donated to help boost the fundraising total.

They included two tickets worth £100 each for a paranormal investigation at Wincham Hall with The Occult Family.

Gemma Nuttall and her tarot reading

Other prizes included a Para-Northern hoodie, a book about Mill Street Barracks and a £35 voucher from Crystalised by Gem.

Para-Northern Investigations was founded in 2017 and has since carried out paranormal investigations at locations in Bolton and further afield.
